headline: Use the simplest automation that does the job.
intro: Not every task needs AI. Simple tools are cheaper, faster and easier to trust. rAIght helps you pick one, and flags AI that keeps repeating itself.

how.title: Choose
how.text: Answer three questions. rAIght suggests the simplest tool.

how.title: Watch
how.text: See what each automation uses and which ones repeat themselves.

how.title: Improve
how.text: Swap a repeating AI for a simple workflow, or switch off what nobody uses.

ladder_intro: Six ways to automate a task. Start at the bottom: each step up costs more.

workflow.plain: A fixed to-do list that runs by itself.

classic_ml.plain: A program that learned from past data.

genai_call.plain: One question to an AI that reads or writes text.

agent.plain: An AI that plans its own steps and uses tools.

multi_agent.plain: Several agents handing work to each other.

terms.meaning: What AI usage is measured in, roughly a short word. More tokens, more cost and energy.
How smart an automation is, from 1 (rule) to 6 (team of agents). Lower is cheaper.
An AI that plans its own steps. Powerful, but the most expensive.
An agent that takes the same steps almost every time. A workflow would do it for less.
Share of runs with identical steps. Above 80 %, an agent is flagged as uniform.
A case an automation could not handle, passed to a person.
The automatic record of each run. rAIght reads it, and no extra AI checks it.
The tool an automation is built in, such as Copilot Studio or n8n.
